doc:
Evaluate a function at an argument. Useful if you want to talk about the partially applied
`Function.eval x : (∀ x, β x) → β x`.
statement: {α : Sort u_1} → {β : α → Sort u_4} → (x : α) → ((x : α) → β x) → β x
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : α → Sort u_4} (x : α) (f : (x : α) → β x), Function.eval x f = f x
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {y : β}, (fun x => y) = Function.const α y
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [Nonempty α], Function.Injective (Function.const α)
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [Nonempty α] {y₁ y₂ : β}, Function.const α y₁ = Function.const α y₂ ↔ y₁ = y₂
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} {b : β}, f = Function.const α b ↔ ∀ (a : α), f a = b

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} (f : β → β → γ) (g : α → β) (a b : α),
  Function.onFun f g a b = f (g a) (g b)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {δ : Sort u_4} (f : α → α → γ) (g : β → α) (h : δ → β),

  Function.onFun f (g ∘ h) = Function.onFun (Function.onFun f g) h

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} (r : β → β → Prop) {f : α → β},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ [Std.Antisymm r], Std.Antisymm (Function.onFun r f)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} (r : β → β → Prop) {f : α → β},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ [Std.Trichotomous r], Std.Trichotomous (Function.onFun r f)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} (r : β → β → Prop) {f : α → β},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ [IsPartialOrder β r], IsPartialOrder α (Function.onFun r f)

  Function.Injective f → ∀ [IsStrictTotalOrder β r], IsStrictTotalOrder α (Function.onFun r f)

∀ {α α' : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} {β' : α' → Sort v} {f : (a : α) → β a} {f' : (a : α') → β' a},
  α = α' → (∀ (a : α) (a' : α'), a ≍ a' → f a ≍ f' a') → f ≍ f'
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : α → Sort u_4} {f₁ f₂ : (a : α) → β a}, f₁ ≠ f₂ ↔ ∃ a, f₁ a ≠ f₂ a
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} [Subsingleton α] {g : α → β} (x y : α), f x = g y ↔ f = g
∀ {α : Type u_4} [inst : LT α], (Function.swap fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2) = fun x1 x2 => x1 > x2
∀ {α : Type u_4} [inst : LE α], (Function.swap fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2) = fun x1 x2 => x1 ≥ x2
∀ {α : Type u_4} [inst : LT α], (Function.swap fun x1 x2 => x1 > x2) = fun x1 x2 => x1 < x2
∀ {α : Type u_4} [inst : LE α], (Function.swap fun x1 x2 => x1 ≥ x2) = fun x1 x2 => x1 ≤ x2
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β}, Function.Bijective f → Function.Injective f
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β}, Function.Bijective f → Function.Surjective f
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β}, ¬Function.Injective f ↔ ∃ a b, f a = f b ∧ a ≠ b
∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Type u_5} [Nontrivial α] {b : β}, ¬Function.Injective fun x => b

doc:
If the co-domain `β` of an injective function `f : α → β` has decidable equality, then
the domain `α` also has decidable equality.
statement: {α : Sort u_1} → {β : Sort u_2} → {f : α → β} → [DecidableEq β] → Function.Injective f → DecidableEq α

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} {g : γ → α},
  Function.Injective (f ∘ g) → Function.Injective g

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β},
  Function.Injective f → ∀ (g : γ → α), Function.Injective (f ∘ g) ↔ Function.Injective g

  (∀ (i : ι), Function.Injective (f i)) → Function.Injective (Pi.map f)

doc: Composition by an injective function on the left is itself injective.
statement: ∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {g : β → γ}, Function.Injective g → Function.Injective fun x => g ∘ x

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} [Nonempty α] {g : β → γ},
  (Function.Injective fun x => g ∘ x) ↔ Function.Injective g
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [Subsingleton α] (f : α → β), Function.Injective f
∀ {α : Sort u_1} [Subsingleton α] (f : α → α), Function.Bijective f

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} (p : α → Prop) [inst : DecidablePred p] {f : { a // p a } → β} {f' : { a // ¬p a } → β},
  Function.Injective f →
    Function.Injective f' →
      (∀ {x x' : α} {hx : p x} {hx' : ¬p x'}, f ⟨x, hx⟩ ≠ f' ⟨x', hx'⟩) →

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} {g : γ → α},
  Function.Surjective (f ∘ g) → Function.Surjective f

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} (f : α → β) {g : γ → α},
  Function.Surjective g → (Function.Surjective (f ∘ g) ↔ Function.Surjective f)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} {g : γ → α},
  Function.Surjective (f ∘ g) → Function.Injective f → Function.Surjective g

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β} {g : γ → α},
  Function.Injective f →
    Function.Injective g → Function.Surjective (f ∘ g) → Function.Bijective f ∧ Function.Bijective g

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β},
  Function.Bijective f → ∀ (g : γ → α), Function.Surjective (f ∘ g) ↔ Function.Surjective g

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β},
  Function.Surjective f → ∀ {p : β → Prop}, (∀ (y : β), p y) ↔ ∀ (x : α), p (f x)

  Function.Surjective f → ∀ {p : β → β → Prop}, (∀ (y₁ y₂ : β), p y₁ y₂) ↔ ∀ (x₁ x₂ : α), p (f x₁) (f x₂)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β},
  Function.Surjective f →
    ∀ {p : β → β → β → Prop}, (∀ (y₁ y₂ y₃ : β), p y₁ y₂ y₃) ↔ ∀ (x₁ x₂ x₃ : α), p (f x₁) (f x₂) (f x₃)
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β}, Function.Surjective f → ∀ {p : β → Prop}, (∃ y, p y) ↔ ∃ x, p (f x)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β},
  Function.Surjective f → ∀ {p : β → β → Prop}, (∃ y₁ y₂, p y₁ y₂) ↔ ∃ x₁ x₂, p (f x₁) (f x₂)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β},
  Function.Surjective f → ∀ {p : β → β → β → Prop}, (∃ y₁ y₂ y₃, p y₁ y₂ y₃) ↔ ∃ x₁ x₂ x₃, p (f x₁) (f x₂) (f x₃)
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} {f : α → β}, Function.Surjective f → Function.Injective fun g => g ∘ f

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} {γ : Type u_4} [Nontrivial γ],

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β}, (∀ (g₁ g₂ : β → Prop), g₁ ∘ f = g₂ ∘ f → g₁ = g₂) → Function.Surjective f

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} (f : α → β), Function.Bijective f ↔ ∀ (b : β), ∃! a, f a = b

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β}, Function.Bijective f → ∀ {p : β → Prop}, (∃! y, p y) ↔ ∃! x, p (f x)

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {γ : Sort u_3} (f : α → β) {g : γ → α},

doc:
If `f : α → α → β` is surjective, then every endofunction on `β` has a fixed point.
This is an instance of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem applied to the category of types
and functions. It is the diagonal argument underlying `cantor_surjective` and
`cantor_injective`.
statement: ∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Type u_5} (f : α → α → β), Function.Surjective f → ∀ (g : β → β), ∃ x, g x = x

doc:
**Cantor's diagonal argument** implies that there are no surjective functions from `α`
to `Set α`.
statement: ∀ {α : Type u_4} (f : α → Set α), ¬Function.Surjective f

doc:
**Cantor's diagonal argument** implies that there are no injective functions from `Set α`
to `α`.
statement: ∀ {α : Type u_4} (f : Set α → α), ¬Function.Injective f

doc:
There is no surjection from `α : Type u` into `Type (max u v)`. This theorem
demonstrates why `Type : Type` would be inconsistent in Lean.
statement: ∀ {α : Type u} (f : α → Type (max u v)), ¬Function.Surjective f

doc:
`g` is a partial inverse to `f` (an injective but not necessarily
surjective function) if `g y = some x` implies `f x = y`, and `g y = none`
implies that `y` is not in the range of `f`.
statement: {α : Type u_4} → {β : Sort u_5} → (α → β) → (β → Option α) → Prop
∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Sort u_5} {f : α → β} {g : β → Option α}, Function.IsPartialInv f g → ∀ (x : α), g (f x) = some x

∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Sort u_5} {f : α → β} {g : β → Option α},
  Function.IsPartialInv f g → ∀ (x : β) (h : (g x).isSome = true), f ((g x).get h) = x

∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Sort u_5} {f : α → β} {g : β → Option α},
  Function.IsPartialInv f g → ∀ (x : α), Function.Surjective fun x_1 => (g x_1).getD x
∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Sort u_5} {f : α → β} {g : β → Option α}, Function.IsPartialInv f g → Function.Injective f

∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Sort u_5} {f : α → β} {g : β → Option α},
  Function.IsPartialInv f g → ∀ (x y : β), ∀ b ∈ g x, b ∈ g y → x = y

∀ {α : Type u_4} {β : Type u_5} {γ : Sort u_6} {f : α → β} {g : β → Option α} {h : β → γ} {i : γ → Option β},
  Function.IsPartialInv f g → Function.IsPartialInv h i → Function.IsPartialInv (h ∘ f) fun x => (i x).bind g

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {g : β → α} {f : α → β}, Function.RightInverse g f → ∀ (x : β), f (g x) = x
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α}, Function.LeftInverse f g → f ∘ g = id
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α}, Function.LeftInverse f g ↔ f ∘ g = id
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α}, Function.RightInverse f g → g ∘ f = id
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} {f : α → β} {g : β → α}, Function.RightInverse f g ↔ g ∘ f = id

doc:
We can use choice to construct explicitly a partial inverse for
a given injective function `f`.

doc:
The inverse of a function (which is a left inverse if `f` is injective
and a right inverse if `f` is surjective).
statement: {α : Sort u} → {β : Sort u_3} → [Nonempty α] → (α → β) → β → α
∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [inst : Nonempty α] {f : α → β} {b : β}, (∃ a, f a = b) → f (Function.invFun f b) = b
∀ {α : Type u_3} {β : Type u_4} {f : α → β} {a : α}, f (Function.invFun f (f a)) = f a

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [inst : Nonempty α] {f : α → β} {b : β},
  (¬∃ a, f a = b) → Function.invFun f b = Classical.choice inst

  Function.Injective f → Function.RightInverse g f → Function.invFun f = g

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [inst : Nonempty α] {f : α → β},
  Function.Surjective f → Function.RightInverse (Function.invFun f) f

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [inst : Nonempty α] {f : α → β},
  Function.Injective f → Function.LeftInverse (Function.invFun f) f

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [inst : Nonempty α] {f : α → β},

∀ {α : Sort u_1} {β : Sort u_2} [Nonempty α] {f : α → β}, Function.Injective f → Function.HasLeftInverse f

doc:
The inverse of a surjective function. (Unlike `invFun`, this does not require
`α` to be inhabited.)
statement: {α : Sort u} → {β : Sort v} → {f : α → β} → Function.Surjective f → β → α
∀ {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {f : α → β} (h : Function.Surjective f) (b : β), f (Function.surjInv h b) = b

∀ {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} [na : Nonempty α] [Subsingleton β] (f : α → β), Function.Surjective f
∀ {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} [Nonempty α] [Subsingleton α] [Subsingleton β] (f : α → β), Function.Bijective f

∀ {ι : Sort u_1} {α : ι → Sort u_2} {β : ι → Sort u_3} {f : (i : ι) → α i → β i},

doc: Composition by a surjective function on the left is itself surjective.
statement: ∀ {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {γ : Sort w} {g : β → γ}, Function.Surjective g → Function.Surjective fun x => g ∘ x

∀ {ι : Sort u_1} {α : ι → Sort u_2} {β : ι → Sort u_3} {f : (i : ι) → α i → β i},

statement: ∀ {α : Sort u} {β : Sort v} {γ : Sort w} {g : β → γ}, Function.Bijective g → Function.Bijective fun x => g ∘ x

doc: Replacing the value of a function at a given point by a given value.
statement: {α : Sort u} → {β : α → Sort v} → [DecidableEq α] → ((a : α) → β a) → (a' : α) → β a' → (a : α) → β a

∀ {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} [inst : DecidableEq α] (a : α) (v : β a) (f : (a : α) → β a),
  Function.update f a v a = v

∀ {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} [inst : DecidableEq α] {a a' : α},
  a ≠ a' → ∀ (v : β a') (f : (a : α) → β a), Function.update f a' v a = f a

doc:
A congruence lemma for `Function.update`, specialized for the non-dependent case. Without this,
`simp` can't rewrite in the fourth argument `a` because the result type depends on `a`.
See also https://github.com/leanprover/lean4/issues/12478.
statement:
∀ {α : Sort u} [inst : DecidableEq α] {β : Sort u_1} {f₁ f₂ : α → β},
  f₁ = f₂ →
    ∀ {a'₁ a'₂ : α},
      a'₁ = a'₂ →
        ∀ {v₁ v₂ : β}, v₁ = v₂ → ∀ {a₁ a₂ : α}, a₁ = a₂ → Function.update f₁ a'₁ v₁ a₁ = Function.update f₂ a'₂ v₂ a₂

doc: On non-dependent functions, `Function.update` can be expressed as an `ite`
statement:
∀ {α : Sort u} [inst : DecidableEq α] {β : Sort u_1} (f : α → β) (a' : α) (b : β) (a : α),
  Function.update f a' b a = if a = a' then b else f a

∀ {α : Sort u} {α' : Sort w} [inst : DecidableEq α] [Subsingleton α] (a : α) (v : α') (f : α → α'),
  Function.update f a v = Function.const α v
∀ {α : Sort u} {β : α → Sort v} [h : ∀ (a : α), Nonempty (β a)] (a : α), Function.Surjective (Function.eval a)

doc:
Recursors can be pushed inside `Function.update`.

The `ctor` argument should be a one-argument constructor like `Sum.inl`,
and `recursor` should be an inductive recursor partially applied in all but that constructor,
such as `(Sum.rec · g)`.

In future, we should build some automation to generate applications like `Option.rec_update` for all
inductive types.
statement:
∀ {ι : Sort u_1} {κ : Sort u_2} {α : κ → Sort u_3} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : DecidableEq κ] {ctor : ι → κ},
  Function.Injective ctor →
    ∀ (recursor : ((i : ι) → α (ctor i)) → (i : κ) → α i),
      (∀ (f : (i : ι) → α (ctor i)) (i : ι), recursor f (ctor i) = f i) →
        (∀ (f₁ f₂ : (i : ι) → α (ctor i)) (k : κ), (∀ (i : ι), ctor i ≠ k) → recursor f₁ k = recursor f₂ k) →
          ∀ (f : (i : ι) → α (ctor i)) (i : ι) (x : α (ctor i)),

doc:
Extension of a function `g : α → γ` along a function `f : α → β`.

For every `a : α`, `f a` is sent to `g a`. `f` might not be surjective, so we use an auxiliary
function `j : β → γ` by sending `b : β` not in the range of `f` to `j b`. If you do not care about
the behavior outside the range, `j` can be used as a junk value by setting it to be `0` or
`Classical.arbitrary` (assuming `γ` is nonempty).

This definition is mathematically meaningful only when `f a₁ = f a₂ → g a₁ = g a₂` (spelled
`g.FactorsThrough f`). In particular this holds if `f` is injective.

A typical use case is extending a function from a subtype to the entire type. If you wish to extend
`g : {b : β // p b} → γ` to a function `β → γ`, you should use `Function.extend Subtype.val g j`.
statement: {α : Sort u_1} → {β : Sort u_2} → {γ : Sort u_3} → (α → β) → (α → γ) → (β → γ) → β → γ

  Function.extend f g e' b = if h : ∃ a, f a = b then g (Classical.choose h) else e' b
